summary: Tchefuncte River Range Lights, Madisonville, Louisiana: a brick tower on Lake Pontchartrain, lit by 1838; rebuilt after the Civil War; unmanned in 1939; town-owned since 1999.

corrections.why: The front range light was activated 30 April 1903 (LighthouseFriends); the record gives no date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NRHP says ten lamps and a fifth-order lens in 1838; LighthouseFriends says nine lamps, a tower built in 1837, and a fifth-order lens installed in 1857. The story reports both.
NRHP says rebuilding was completed in early 1868; LighthouseFriends says the fifth-order lens was first shown on 1 December 1867.

LighthouseFriends says July 1915. The Light-House Service bulletin describes the New Orleans hurricane of 29 September 1915 and commends Keeper Groux for it. Story follows the bulletin and notes the disagreement.
LighthouseFriends says the last keeper left in 1939 and the light was solarized in 1952; the station record says automated 1952. Story gives both dates.

notes_for_editor: (1) Lamp count (10 NRHP, 9 LighthouseFriends), the first-light year (1838 NRHP vs tower built 1837 LF) and the year of the fifth-order lens (1838 NRHP vs 1857 LF) are unresolved; story gives both. (2) Height: NRHP 1886 light list gives a 34-foot tower; LighthouseFriends 36 feet (1837); USLHS 43 ft (13.1 m) tower height and 48 ft focal height; the record has 13.1 m and focal 7.6 m. Unresolved. (3) The 1915 Bulletin's damage list is OCR-garbled, so the damage claim rests on the 1912-1917 index entry 'Chefuncte River light station damaged by hurricane' (p. 186 of the bulletin). (4) The 1920 towed steamship's name is garbled in the OCR and is not given. (5) The 1923 raft date is 17 May as the Bulletin gives it, year taken from the 1923 volume. (6) The 1926 Bulletin spells the station 'Chefulicte River' in OCR; the story uses the standard spelling. (7) Chronicling America search 'Chefuncte' (LA, 1888) returned nothing; the 1888 storm rests on the NRHP and LighthouseFriends. (8) The Fox 8 article has no byline in the cached copy. The Maritime Museum page is promotional: only facts and two short phrases are used. (9) Access: LighthouseFriends says best viewed by boat; no source gives today's public visiting arrangements for the tower. (10) Roster: 22 lines, including an acting keeper, Louis G. Laborie (1911). The roster is the archive's own text; the person slugs are on the archive's lines. (11) Fact-check 2026-10-22: re-read against the NRHP nomination, LighthouseFriends, the 1915, 1920, 1923 and 1926 Bulletins (PDF pp. 40, 41, 23, 26, 39 confirmed by corpus.py page), the 1918 Commissioner's report (printed p. 42, scan 356, confirmed), the 1912-1917 and 1918-1923 index pages, the USLHS roster (22 lines, 1837-1939, confirmed), the Fox 8 article and the Maritime Museum page. (12) Not reconciled: the 1915 hurricane date. The Bulletin's text gives 'At New Orleans on September 29' (PDF p. 40); a commendation list (PDF p. 43) refers to 'the hurricane of September 28-29'; LighthouseFriends dates a hurricane at the station to July 1915. The story gives 29 September and LighthouseFriends' July date. (13) The 1920 towed steamship's name is OCR-garbled and is not given; the 'disabled' wording is quoted as the OCR prints it. (14) The 2004 donor is not named in the story. (15) The Fox 8 groundbreaking was on Tuesday, 29 October 2024 (the story gives the date); the story does not say the project sits 'near the tower', since the article does not say so.
